findings.where: Nav bar home link (the arch mark and 'MMM INFRA' wordmark), at both widths, and the large white section drawing of the mark in the hero; the palette tile, which does not list either logo colour
findings.fault: The logo appears only in white. Its fixed colours are gone: the grey #404040 arches and the blue #0070C0 wordmark. The diazo-blue ground has about the same lightness as the logo blue, so the full-colour logo cannot sit on this ground at all. Mark does not hold a white version, and nothing records his agreement to one. The palette neither takes the logo blue and grey as tokens nor marks them logo-only, so the identity gives the real logo nowhere to live across the whole site.
findings.who_objects: Mark. Rule 7 says the logo stays, and the brief says it is never redrawn. Here his blue-and-grey mark becomes a white one on every page without his approval. A visitor who knows MMM Infra's blue wordmark from his current site or his documents would see a different-coloured logo.

findings.where: Article specimen ('The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law': body paragraphs, pull quote and PDF link card) at both widths
findings.fault: The article prose sits on the same busy blueprint ground as the hero: a two-weight grid of light lines runs straight through the glyphs of long body text. The tile has no plainer reading surface for Read mode. Any PDF thumbnail or photograph Angélique adds to a post would also sit on this gridded, saturated blue, with nothing designed to hold it.
findings.who_objects: Development-bank staff reading one of Mark's articles to the end: the grid crossing every line makes a long read tiring. Angélique would also object: client value 9 asks that the look survive a lay editor adding posts and PDFs, and this ground gives her uploads no neutral place to sit.

findings.where: Hero drawing: the amber hatch in the third arch, beside the amber 'WRITE TO MARK' button; the palette's 'Sodium amber' swatch ('daylight in the drawing, and the one action')
findings.fault: The one contrasting hue has two jobs: lighting a static part of the drawing and marking the only action. The first screen shows two amber areas, so the button no longer stands alone, and the amber bay can read as a highlighted, live part.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor scanning for what to do. With amber both in the drawing and on the button, they get a weaker signal for the one action, getting in touch with Mark.
